I was leading a raid against a human fortress: my legendary warrior and seven of my most powerful vampires fought with all their might against the stronghold. Suddenly I got a message: my lair is under attack. Knights and archers were entering my dungeon, and the weak poison traps didn't really hurt them. Orcs and even the lowly goblins tried to put up a fight, but were cut down mercilessly by the knights. A few of the vampires had more success against the intruders, killing a few. A vampire's head was chopped, yet it kept fighting, swinging wildly. Ultimately the knights were victorious. Not much was between them and the Keeper of the Lair. I controlled the keeper, stunning them, buffing myself, fighting down an archer, stunning another knight in a hallway so the others cannot enter, then blinking away before they were able to catch me. But they kept coming, and my spells were all on cooldown. I fled to a long corridor, hoping to win some time... I was prepared to die, yet the knights seemed to lost me. I gave up the direct control of the Keeper, to see what happened. It seemed that all the knights surrendered, and were heading to the prison! But why? And then I noticed that my legendary warrior returned to the keep from the siege. The knights knew that they had no chance. Phew. Another crisis gone. Then, because of the corpses lying around, poisonous gases polluted the air, and I died. Roguelike at its best.

很好玩的游戏，作为一个曾经着迷于DUNGENKEEPER的玩家，我表示这个游戏非常值得尝试（虽然，并没有DK那种搞怪的剧情） 更新线----2016.2.22 最近闲着没事，又来玩了玩。（作者之前放了两个月的假） 本次更新以后，玩家们可以安心的BUILD&TRAINING了，敌对AI不再玩了命的往你家里冲（当然，旧版本往你家里冲也没关系，就算是送钱了）。 玩家通过侦查类动物（秃鹫、穴居熊、野狼等）或者自己控制怪物来发现文明，还可以通过招募来从友好文明里添加特定怪物（暂时用处不大，因为玩家的房间会自己吸引怪物）。 为各种动作添加音效（其实之前光是只有背景音乐就能玩很久了），添加楼梯（增加探索乐趣）。 现在有哪些物种跟你敌对会显示在你的怪物页面，编队更加便捷（不过得稍微熟悉一下是托哪里，不然搞半天弄不明白） 更新线----2016.8.7 过了很久没玩，最近手痒，又下下来开了一盘。 增加，多了一个Champain模式，姑且可以认为是任务模式。为什么说是“姑且”，因为，你要做的是，定制自己的敌人，定制自己的同盟，然后，选择你想选择的敌对地牢，然后把它们roll在一张策略地图上。之后，选择你自己的地盘，开始养怪物、进攻和被进攻的领主人生吧。 +充分利用队伍集结 +前期不会再有傻瓜给你送金子了(对于门口陷阱流) +晚上去中立或者友善地图搜刮劫掠再也不是难题，再也不用担心绕路和家里被A -侦察兵在这种模式下意义不大，可以拿去献祭或者主动投敌了XD 然后现在的succubus和你城（洞穴）里的怪物XXOO之后会给怪物上buff（鞭挞也有同样的效果，不过那个之前的版本已经有了2月份那阵） tips：不要觉得你的领主就是一辈子啃书的命，魔法学完了让他去训练场，制造魔力的事情交给兽人巫师。(然后，你的敌对势力欢欢喜喜的冲过了你的防线——对，我说的是陷阱流。结果发现你家领主一夫当关把它们都杀跑了) tips：这游戏的正确打开方式是，设定好房间，然后，可以选择挂机（等魔法和怪物等级），也可以主动出去刚（最好黑天，魔法双倍），或者一波一波的送怪（你要是前期主巢穴，出怪兽快，可以这么玩） tips：工坊一定不要造太多，不然会给你很多小各布林，很占人口也没有物理输出。 tips：要让你家领主进行训练，选中到信息面板以后把研究的钩去钓，再切换一下当前状态变成训练。 tips：空格暂停，1234调整速度，鼠标滚轮支持画面缩放。 另外，就目前而言，我觉得完成度完全已经很高了。

As one review succinctly put it, KeeperRL is "Dwarf Fortress for sane people." Let me expand on that. Dwarf Fortress is a game I love to read about. You get such awesome stories from it, like [url=http://www.timdenee.com/bronzemurder/]Bronzemurder[/url] (one of the more succinct, well-presented ones). I've always loved reading DF stories. But when I try playing it, even after sinking 20 hours into playing and working through tutorials, I'm still quite baffled by what to do, why things happen, or how to get things done. I've never had a functioning Fortress. I've never been able to figure out how to brew booze (which Dwarves need for life, like water). I think it has something to do with plants I have to grow, but I can't figure out what plants, how to grow them, etc etc. Enter KeeperRL. After 20 MINUTES into KeeperRL, I have a (rather haphazard, admittedly) [strike]fortress[/strike] [i]dungeon[/i]. It works. It functions. The game prompted me on the very basics I'd need. If I wanted to deviate from that, it let me; it even lets me turn off those hints... but it didn't assume, from the get-go, that I wasn't a new player. It never assumed that I wanted to spend as much time researching this game as it takes to write a college paper just to be able to play the game on the most basic level. That's important in such a complex game! The Dwarf Fortress game cycles like this: Play, Die, Boggle, Google. Repeat. But KeeperRL cycles in like this instead: Play, Die, LEARN. Repeat. That makes it, even in this Alpha state, far more enjoyable than the glorious complexity of one of its main inspirations, Dwarf Fortress. TL;DR, yes, KeeperRL is DF for sane people.

非常非常非常非常好玩！强烈推荐这款游戏！ 我是种田/建筑/经营/历史/策略/休闲玩家。玩过哆啦A梦牧场物语，修仙模拟器，rimworld，饥荒，缺氧，动物园之星，城市:天际线，Parkitect, 地下城2，地下城3，战锤全战等游戏。要我形容，不买这款游戏你肯定会后悔。价格方面它在同类作品里处于较低花费。内容上非常丰富。我见过很多游戏，它们只注意酷炫的画面却忽略了游戏内容，导致玩家玩一两次就没兴趣了。然而这款游戏恰恰好在它的游戏性方面，而且画风也是不错的。因此这款游戏非常耐玩，也非常符合我对于好游戏的期待。我个人认为画面再好的游戏，内容如果糟糕，就不能算一个好的游戏。因为我是要玩游戏而不是看动画。所以，在我看来这是个成功的游戏。在我目前玩过的所有游戏中处于最佳的几个。唯一的遗憾是没有中文，但这并不影响游戏体验。下面具体说说游戏本身： 第一，在这个游戏里你可以扮演地下城领主，建造属于自己的地下城。也可以扮演冒险者去闯地下城。当然你也可以控制小怪去体验小怪是怎么生活的。地下城领主不仅有黑暗魔法师，你甚至可以当人类的领主！ 第二，评论里的一些问题并不存在。比如有人说不能造墙，我试过，可以造。 第三，游戏不大，但内容非常丰富。此外里面的AI做的非常好，智商很高。在这点上得批评修仙模拟器，那款游戏的AI简直是智障，就是因为这点我不再玩那个游戏了。 第四，有复杂的计算系统。每个NPC都有各种属性，还有对于各种地形环境的模拟，代入感很足； 第五，虽然没有中文，但里面的英语词汇不难，很容易看懂； 第六，音乐很棒，数量不多但很不错，其中人类领主的背景音乐充满乡村风味。有种来到中世纪乡下的感觉； 目前发现唯一的问题是全屏显示后鼠标的位置略微偏移。解决的办法是在Setting里先把Full Screen设置成off，然后点击缩小的那个方块，之后再把Full Screen改成on，你会发现问题已经解决。 总结，如果你喜欢地下城，喜欢种田休闲，喜欢规划，喜欢奇幻世界，推荐你入手这款游戏。个人认为即使不打折的时候购买，也是值得的。

Okay now that I've got a good amount of hours under my belt I'm going to suggest that you wait on this. I had fun with it. The foundation is good but it needs to be built up more. Playing as a human keeper destroys fps since you need to recruit farm animals (which act as food supply). My dungeon with 150+ troops also requires about 120+ farm animals and each animal is considered a unit (which each processes its own turn). This excess load, when compared to the evil factions (which only require statues to be constructed to hire more troops), is very noticeable and detracts from gameplay. Frankly, the game is too easy. I put the difficulty to hard and set the waves to constant (or whatever the highest frequency was), but it still was very easy to fend off enemy aggression. There are many QoL issues at hand. You only have 3 Quarters areas to designate and 3 Guard areas to designate so larger dungeons are hampered by this limitation. You cannot tell where a character is located without pressing the locate button (I wish that the Z-level would display on their character card). Inventory management is a nightmare, especially considering high Z-level dungeons. Units often use scrolls of weapon enhancement or defense (very important end game items) on ♥♥♥♥♥♥ gear without you being notified. When clicking on 'Add consumable', not all consumables in the dungeon are listed. Melee is the only viable option in the game because of a bug with arrow cooldowns going to obscenely high rates. I think this game's saving grace (and most unique feature) is that you can fight against other people's dungeons. This means that when you are making your own dungeon, it is not only for yourself, but for someone else to eventually play through. A very cool concept that I hope gets expanded in the future. I'll say again, I had fun with it, but there is a lot that is missing here, and it does need to be addressed for a more enjoyable experience. If you can't wait, you'll still have fun, but realize this game is not finished.

As much as I respect small works of passion like this I need to give this a not recommended for a number of reasons. 1. The UI is god awful. Few games are worse in this regard. 2. The game as a whole, and the combat system is quite simple, but made frustratingly awkward to interact with by the janky UI. This is only a separate item from #1 to point out that however bad the interface normally is, it's way worse in combat. 3. Balance and progression are very rough. Power curves are quite sudden. You could get attacked early by an ogre and find that your 8 some units just get wrecked without barely leaving a scratch. Or you might get into the game a bit, be stomping everything without concern, but then get attacked by the humans who then totally annihilate you. It's not that it's hard, it's that the game doesn't communicate the threat, or ramp in a way that feels intuitive. I'm a fan of similar games, but ultimately just didn't find this deep enough or polished enough to hold my interest.

I purchased this game in EA YEARS ago, because I loved the concept and wanted to support the dev. I'm going to preface this negative review with the caveat that I'm sure hardcore fans of Dwarf-Fortress type games will LOVE this. If that sounds like you, definitely buy this game! This review is for the rest of us normies who are thinking about dipping their toes into the genre. This game is not Dungeons, or Dungeon Keeper, so if that's what you're thinking think again. Firstly, after years in EA it's finally in full release, but there's clearly some parts of the game that just aren't done. The most glaring one you'll run into is the fact that you'll KNOW you have to do something to progress (In some cases, the game will tell you so), but you'll have absolutely no clue how to get it done. The game encyclopedia is very limited. You'll get notifications that certain of your creatures need personal quarters, but GFL figuring out how to do that. Google it? Nah, you'll just find a couple forum threads of people saying they figured it out, but didn't think to tell us how. 6hrs into my first playthrough, my base is attacked by a dragon (Why, and how, IDFK), and he appears in my keepers bedroom, immediately one-shots him, and my game is over. Sweet.,, Great FU to a player who is really trying to learn the ropes. Overall, I don't regret supporting this dev, but I can't recommend what this game turned into to the vast majority of general strategy game players.

Game 1: I have no idea what I'm doing and get killed by a deer...yes, a deer....within five minutes. Game 2: Still clueless, I fumble about for an hour and am just beginning to get a handle on things until dwarves attack from out of nowhere and we're on to... Game 3: Many hours in and my dungeon is a powerhouse. I misclick on the recruiting tab and invite an insane werewolf in. At night. He guts me like a fish and suddenly I'm choosing to begin... Game 4: The game suddenly seems set to easy. I have every resource in abundance, battles are effortless, and luck itself seems to be my minion. I'm the baddest keeper on the block until a farmer one-shots me in the neck. Well, I definitely won't be taking my keeper into battle when I restart... Game 5: The game I'll fondly remember as "Surprise...It's a Bear!". Once they get a taste for imp it's just a matter of time until you're moving on to... Games 6 and 7: Necromancy isn't easy, kids. If two games in twenty minutes taught me anything it was that. Oh, well. There's always... Game 8: ..and now I'm...er, was... the kind of lich that could raise the Titanic. My undead spread like locusts from our mountain safehold and the world's nights were filled with terror. I, however, was not afraid enough and now my keeper is just a greasy, smoking stain on the mountainside. I hope zombies give dragons terrible indigestion. My first day with this game saw me lose eight times, sometimes badly, and I'm still chomping at the bit to start the ninth. This game is just so much fun. The dev took the best bits and pieces from other great games, blended them together with a pinch of brutal RNG, and delivered a high quality effort with a charm and identity all its own. I have some really great games in my collection and just a couple hours, this was already one of my favorites. I could go on and on and on but it's time to see what game 9 holds. Even if it's a cyclops fifteen minutes in, it's going to be fun!

Interesting game. I mix of Rimworld and Dungeon Keeper. I like it, will keep playing it, but in it's current state I cannot recommend it to others. This is due to two main issues. Poor execution and game breaking imbalance. Software wise, the game functions fine. It doesn't crash or erroneously remove/corrupt a saved game. Commands are followed. It works. It's the explanations...of HOW the game works that is what is wrong. That is the easy yet tedious part of the development. Documentation. Why am I 20 hours into the game and can't figure out were the resource are that I need to move forward??? There's is a system to capture monsters and people. Awesome! Under "help" it shows that you can right-click and give orders to capture people...and then tells you you need to make them weak by attacking them until they are unconscious. Awesome x2!! Done it....so why are they just laying there unconscious on the ground? How do we collect them? Isn't an Imp supposed to pick them up and take them back to base? .....oh there's a "Prison" system in the build menus. Maybe I need that.....wait I can't build any other the Prison items..why not?? Oh...it looks like they need Iron Ore to be built...ok..well..where do I find Iron Ore??......*checks help*....*checks Tutorial*....*checks for Manual*....there is no explanation on where to find Iron Ore. Not only that but I need Iron Ore in order to make new weapons and upgrade almost all aspects of my base. ..So..why is there no mention of how to acquire it???? You can see the problem here. If it was just one system or a smaller system unexplained then it could just be an oversight...but this issue keep occurring. "Oh look a Harpy is showing available to be recruited... Great..but why? How do I get more creatures to show up for recruitment? The peasants in the village show a "hostile" flag...but they don't attack me? The Leader has a message that says "Immigration will stop if killed'..?? What the heck does that mean? Immigration is the way you recruit monsters...does this mean peasants will show up for recruiting??? Why do some NPCs have purple circles around them and other have red ones? *NOT documented anywhere*. This is what I mean by poor execution. This is what leads to being 20hrs into the game and struggling to move forward. I eventually found a comment by someone saying they figured out if you just dig down you'll find iron. Awesome...why isn't that statement in a help section or documented somewhere? *load game, digs down two level, ..see's new granite..but no Iron* How far down do I have to dig? Why is this a thing? My bases fit just fine on two different levels of the map. *shrug* Other issue, imbalances. I've played two games, classic mode. The 1st started me off between a hydra, giant ants, cyclops and some Dryad and Elves. I killed off the ants and cyclops....but I can't damage the Hydra with my Goblin warriors and Wizards. So now my influence sphere ONLY..allows me to move into the Dryads and Elves. Well the Elves are too high level so I visit the dryads and find that they kill everything in a few shots without being visible behind trees. Turns out...they're Elves...and from what I read on the forums they're just broken and kill everything faster than any boss creatures in the game. ....I build and send multiple parties of Goblins that just die/get captured almost instantly. I can't advance my influence sphere.....the game is now at a halt. Must start new game.. New game starts me next to Elves, Dryads, and a few extras.....

It's a nice little game, HOWEVER, don't be fooled by the state of release. This game is missing a crazy amount of features and is still pretty much in an early early access state. Recommended: No I really wanted to like KeeperRL, but after climbing the initial learning curve, the game quickly started to feel like an exhausting chore rather than a fun, relaxing escape. A few things that ultimately led to me uninstalling: * Misleading UI & Mechanics: The game does a poor job of explaining its own tools. For example, the "Crafting" menu icon looks exactly like a zone brush tile, which led to me accidentally building 14 individual crafting stations instead of designating a single room zone. The vanilla lack of basic features like natural tree regrowth also feels weirdly static, even if mods can fix it. * Menu Overload: The core gameplay relies heavily on dense menu digging, micro-managing individual character sheets, and endless reading. It stays highly mechanical throughout, and if you don't enjoy fighting the interface, the loop doesn't change or get any better later on. * Grating Audio: If you build a functional training or research setup, your magic-using minions will constantly level up. This triggers a repetitive, back-to-back evil cackling/laughing sound effect loop that will drive you up the wall very quickly. If you enjoy highly meticulous, menu-driven management games where you don't mind fighting the UI, there is a deep system here. But if you want a smooth, rewarding dungeon builder to unwind with after a long day, this one might just feel like a second shift at a data entry desk.

I wanted to like KeeperRL because the concept is great: build an evil dungeon, recruit minions, and grow your power like a proper Dungeon Keeper-style game. Unfortunately, the game keeps getting in its own way. I tried a Necromancer run, where corpses/remains are a core resource for making more undead, but my minions simply would not reliably collect them even after I had the proper storage set up. The only dependable solution was to manually take control of a minion and haul the bodies myself before they rotted or became unusable. That is not fun. That is busywork. A game like this should make basic resource collection reliable, especially when that resource is central to an entire playstyle. I do not mind complexity, but I do mind having to fight the game’s automation just to make the main mechanics work. Cool idea, but too clunky and frustrating for me to recommend.

KeeperRL occupies a totally unique space in the industry because it makes a fusion that no other developer has tried: it takes the dungeon-building and vision (Dungeon Keeper/War for the Overworld style), adds simplified colony management (Dwarf Fortress style) and ties it all together with map exploration and roguelike combat (where you control the villain in turns to destroy villages and fight enemies of your faction). This triple mix is ​​exclusive to it. I searched and couldn't find another game with these combined mechanics because I wanted to play more games like this, if anyone knows of others, please comment =) FYI: There's so much untapped potential in this niche; the creator could add more activities to the map, random encounters, and events...lots of things.
